headline: Structure-derived inputs drive learned binding and affinity prediction across targets
label: Structure Aware Affinity Prediction
summary: Recent items pair 3D structure and protein language model embeddings with conformal and positive-unlabeled learning for interaction and affinity prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is coupling structure-derived or structure-informed inputs with learned scoring for binding, interaction, and affinity prediction. DESTIN predicts compound-protein interactions genome-wide from 3D compound and protein structures using a fine-tuned 3D foundation model. CrossMol pre-trains by reconstructing missing 3D molecular structure guided by SMILES semantics. Other items rely on sequence, language-model, or graph representations: the GPCR multitask GNN fuses ligand graphs with frozen protein language model embeddings, Katalyst aligns enzyme sequences with protein text for kcat prediction, and RCP-DTA adds sample-specific conformal intervals to drug-target affinity. Distinct here is the use of a 3D foundation model for genome-scale interaction prediction, alongside attention to uncertainty and to leakage, as the enzyme-substrate study reports similarity-driven inflation of model performance.
